analysis:
The change in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift is small. In unloadModel (head ~1133-1137), a successful Nemotron Super retirement now calls selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue(now: .now). The same call is added at the end of the normal unload path (head ~1203), after retryReserveDeferredPrefetches(). The effect is that selected models waiting on capacity are re-checked at the next capacity tick instead of waiting out their backoff.

Security-relevant observations:
- The change touches no cryptography, attestation, serving authorization (A-016/T-053), prefix-cache storage (T-041), or key material.
- The recovery path still goes through ensureModelLoaded, which retains its existing gates: autopilotServesModel, runtime eligibility, retiring checks, and the weight-hash and TOCTOU bracketing for SSD-reusable loads. makeAllDue only schedules a retry, so those gates are not bypassed.
- Availability: eviction or idle-timeout unloads can now trigger an immediate reload attempt. This could in theory cause load/unload churn (T-016/T-029 class, memory thrash). It is bounded because the call fires only on successful unloads, and loads are serialized by the isLoadingAny gate and memory admission. The supplied evidence does not show an unbounded loop. If recovery loads an evicted model and that evicts another, a ping-pong is possible. Whether selectedModelRecovery enforces per-model rate limiting or a cap is outside the supplied source.
- Sequencing is unchanged: the new call runs after the cache purge, slot removal and capacity update, so no ordering regression is visible in the supplied excerpt.

Open question for integration: the implementation of selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue and its tick consumer is not in the supplied evidence. Next review should confirm it respects the load gate, the allowEviction=false posture for recovery, and rate limits.
